result.topic_en: Euler shows that, modulo a prime of the form 4n+1, fourth powers leave the same residues as squares when n is odd, and derives corollaries about quadruples of biquadrates with equal residues and the roots of x^4-1.
result.transcription:
126 RESIDVA EX DIVIS. POTESTATVM
eadem residua praebent atque $a^2$, $a^6$, $a^{10}$ etc. vnde his interpolatis oritur progressio
$1, a^2, a^4, a^6, a^8 \ldots\ldots\ldots a^{8n}$
quae eadem residua dat, ac progressio numerorum quadratorum. Ex biquadratis ergo hoc casu eadem plane residua omnia nascuntur atque ex ipsis quadratis.
Coroll. 1.
81. Si ergo numeri biquadrati per numerum primum formae $4n+1$ diuidantur, tantum $n$ residua diuersa oriuntur, vnde semper quaterna biquadrata dantur $p^4$, $q^4$, $r^4$, $s^4$, quorum radices diuisore sunt minores, quae per $4n+1$ diuisa idem praebeant residuum; vbi quidem perspicuum est fore $s=-p$ et $r=-q$ seu quod eodem redit $s=4n+1-p$ et $r=4n+1-q$. Hinc istae formulae $p+q+r+s$; $p^2+q^2+r^2+s^2$ et $p^3+q^3+r^3+s^3$ per $4n+1$ erunt diuisibiles.
Coroll. 2.
82. Quaterna ergo biquadrata, quae per numerum primum $4n+1$ diuisa vnitatem relinquent, erunt valores ipsius $x$, quibus formula $x^4-1$ per $4n+1$ fit diuisibilis, vnde primo est $x=1$, tum si alius valor sit $x=b$, erit quoque $x=b^2$ et $x=b^3$; neque vltra progredi opus est, quia $b^4$ vnitati aequiualet.
Coroll. 3.

items.quote: Ex biquadratis ergo hoc casu eadem plane residua omnia nascuntur atque ex ipsis quadratis.
items.english: Therefore in this case exactly the same residues arise from the biquadrates as from the squares themselves.

items.quote: Hinc istae formulae $p+q+r+s$; $p^2+q^2+r^2+s^2$ et $p^3+q^3+r^3+s^3$ per $4n+1$ erunt diuisibiles.
items.english: Hence the formulas p+q+r+s, p^2+q^2+r^2+s^2 and p^3+q^3+r^3+s^3 will be divisible by 4n+1.

items.quote: vnde primo est $x=1$, tum si alius valor sit $x=b$, erit quoque $x=b^2$ et $x=b^3$; neque vltra progredi opus est, quia $b^4$ vnitati aequiualet.
items.english: whence first x=1, then if another value is x=b, also x=b^2 and x=b^3; there is no need to go further, since b^4 is equivalent to unity.
